Visit note | 2025-01-11 11:30 AM | Dr. Farhana Kabir, General Medicine | Patient: Ruma Mahmud, 63, female. The patient presented with a sudden high fever, severe aching in her bones and muscles, and a faint rash on her arms. She is a madrasa teacher, and these symptoms started during the monsoon after mosquitoes bred in water tanks near Barishal. She has a history of Hypothyroidism. She denies any spontaneous bleeding, vomiting, or altered consciousness. On examination, her vitals showed a temperature 101.1°F, BP 121/86 mmHg, pulse 105 bpm, weight 93 kg, and her platelet count 99000 per microlitre. Assessment: Dengue fever. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to drink at least three litres of fluid a day, avoid ibuprofen and aspirin, and repeat the platelet count in 48 hours. She must go to the hospital at once if she experiences bleeding gums, black stools, or severe belly pain. Follow-up: 48 hours with a repeat platelet count.

Visit note | 2025-01-11 12:00 PM | Dr. Rokeya Khatun, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Lamia Pramanik, 21, female. The patient reports experiencing discomfort in her lower abdomen along with a burning sensation during urination. She works as a bus driver, and these symptoms began during a hot week with little water intake in Motijheel. She has a known comorbidity of Hypothyroidism. She denies any high fever, chills, flank pain, or vaginal discharge. On physical examination, there was mild suprapubic tenderness, but no costovertebral angle tenderness. Vitals recorded were temperature 98.9°F, BP 116/83 mmHg, pulse 77 bpm, weight 52 kg. Assessment: Uncomplicated urinary tract infection. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to drink at least two litres of water daily and not to hold urine for long. Follow-up: 1 week if symptoms continue.

Visit note | 2025-01-11 03:00 PM | Dr. Habibur Rahman, Orthopedics | Patient: Ishrat Islam, 76, female. The patient presents with complaints of persistent pain in her knees when climbing stairs and mild morning stiffness that lasts only a few minutes. She works as a shopkeeper and reports that the pain has become significantly worse since moving to a building with no lift in Kushtia. No major comorbidities are reported. She denies any joint swelling, redness, warmth, or history of recent trauma. On examination, bilateral crepitus was noted on knee extension. Vitals and measurements: BMI 32.3, BP 135/86 mmHg, pulse 85 bpm, weight 86 kg. Assessment: Knee osteoarthritis. Plan: a prescription was issued. She is advised to do thigh-strengthening exercises daily, lose weight, and avoid squatting and sitting cross-legged on the floor. Follow-up: 6 weeks with physiotherapy.

Visit note | 2025-01-12 02:00 PM | Dr. Arif Hossain, Pulmonology | Patient: Habiba Hossain, 60, female. The patient presented with a high fever and sharp chest pain upon deep inspiration. Interestingly, she presented atypically with prominent belly pain and diarrhoea, accompanied by only a mild cough. She is a photographer, and these symptoms began after caring for a sick relative in Keraniganj. She has no chronic comorbidities. On examination, decreased breath sounds were noted in the right lower lung field. Her vitals were temperature 103.0°F, BP 135/85 mmHg, pulse 96 bpm, SpO2 94%, weight 48 kg. Assessment: Community-acquired pneumonia. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to rest and drink plenty of fluids, and to return at once if breathing becomes difficult. Follow-up: 3 days for review and a chest X-ray in 6 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-01-12 02:00 PM | Dr. Jannatul Ferdous, Orthopedics | Patient: Mostafa Patwary, 26, male. The patient returns for a follow-up visit to review his ongoing ankle pain and localized swelling which continues to limit his walking. He is a bus driver and originally twisted his ankle while stepping off a bus in Mymensingh. There are no comorbidities. He reports no numbness, tingling, or coldness in the toes of the affected foot. Physical examination reveals tenderness over the lateral ligament complex of the ankle and moderate edema, though the joint is stable. Vitals recorded: pain score 8/10, BP 128/83 mmHg, pulse 69 bpm, weight 75 kg. Assessment: Ankle sprain. Plan: a prescription was issued. The patient was advised to follow rest, ice, compression, and elevation (RICE) guidelines for 48 hours and to use a crepe bandage. Follow-up: 1 week.

Visit note | 2025-01-12 02:30 PM | Dr. Rezaul Karim, Neurology | Patient: Masud Siddique, 69, male. The patient describes experiencing numb toes and a burning sensation in both feet, which are notably worse at night. He is a farmer and notes that these symptoms have become worse since walking barefoot at home in Chattogram. His medical history includes Hypothyroidism. He denies any weakness in his legs, difficulty walking, or history of back injury. Neurological exam reveals reduced sensation at 8 of 10 monofilament test sites on both feet. Vitals: BP 124/79 mmHg, pulse 80 bpm, weight 92 kg. Assessment: Peripheral neuropathy. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to check his feet daily for cuts, wear soft closed shoes, and keep his blood sugar under control. Follow-up: 6 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-01-12 02:30 PM | Dr. Shahadat Hossain, ENT | Patient: Faruk Alam, 39, male. The patient presents with nasal congestion and a thick nasal discharge that has lasted for more than ten days. He works as an NGO field officer, and the symptoms started after a cold during a rainy week in Banani. He has a comorbidity of Essential hypertension. He denies having any high fever, vision changes, or severe forehead pain. On examination, there is tenderness over the maxillary sinuses bilaterally. Vitals: temperature 99.5°F, BP 137/93 mmHg, pulse 110 bpm, weight 93 kg. Assessment: Acute sinusitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to use steam inhalation twice daily and drink warm fluids. Follow-up: 10 days.

Visit note | 2025-01-12 03:00 PM | Dr. Tanvir Ahmed, General Medicine | Patient: Taslima Shikder, 55, female. The patient presents with an atypical clinical picture: she complains of a strong craving to chew ice and has a sore, smooth tongue, but reports very little tiredness. She works as a software developer and noticed these changes after months of skipping lunch during long shifts in Gazipur. She has a history of Bronchial asthma. She denies any blood in her stool or dark urine. On examination, she has mild conjunctival pallor and a smooth, erythematous tongue. Vitals and labs: haemoglobin 9.7 g/dL, BP 136/72 mmHg, pulse 76 bpm, weight 61 kg. Assessment: Iron deficiency anaemia. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to eat more lentils, spinach, liver, and eggs, and to avoid drinking tea within an hour of meals. Follow-up: 6 weeks with a repeat haemoglobin.

Visit note | 2025-01-12 03:00 PM | Dr. Imran Kabir, Gastroenterology | Patient: Shamima Karim, 72, female. The patient describes a gnawing pain in her upper abdomen that is relieved by eating but frequently wakes her up at night. She is a retired civil servant, and these symptoms started after weeks of taking painkillers for back pain in Tangail. She has no chronic comorbidities. She denies any vomiting of blood, black tarry stools, or unexplained weight loss. On examination, there is mild epigastric tenderness on deep palpation. Vitals: pain score 7/10, BP 119/86 mmHg, pulse 79 bpm, weight 55 kg. Assessment: Peptic ulcer disease. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to avoid painkillers such as ibuprofen, stop smoking, and eat regular meals. Follow-up: 4 weeks with a stool H. pylori test.

Visit note | 2025-01-12 03:00 PM | Dr. Asif Mahmud, Dermatology | Patient: Khadija Khan, 63, female. The patient presents with itchy skin eruptions that began after consuming a new food, as well as occasional swelling of her lips. She is a farmer and reported that these symptoms started after eating prawns at a restaurant in Bashundhara. She has a history of Bronchial asthma. She denies any shortness of breath, wheezing, or difficulty swallowing. On examination, there are about 36 welts on the trunk and arms, which are erythematous and raised. Vitals: BP 110/84 mmHg, pulse 77 bpm, weight 70 kg. Assessment: Acute urticaria. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to avoid the suspected food, keep a symptom diary, and go to the hospital at once if her tongue or throat swells. Follow-up: 2 weeks with the symptom diary.

Visit note | 2025-01-12 03:30 PM | Dr. Saiful Alam, Endocrinology | Patient: Ishrat Bhuiyan, 35, female. The patient reports unexplained weight loss despite having a good appetite and describes a growing intolerance to heat. She works as a bus driver, and these symptoms began after a stressful family event in Kushtia. She has a history of Hypothyroidism. She denies any visual changes, eye pain, or neck swelling. On examination, a fine tremor was noted in her hands, and mild lid lag was present. Vitals: pulse 122 bpm, BP 130/81 mmHg, weight 84 kg. Assessment: Hyperthyroidism. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to avoid excess tea and coffee and to rest when her heart races. Follow-up: 4 weeks with thyroid function tests.

Visit note | 2025-01-12 04:00 PM | Dr. Anisur Rahman, Ophthalmology | Patient: Emon Dewan, 45, male. The patient complains of a painful, red, swollen lump at the edge of his right eyelid. He is a police constable and notes that the condition began after a dusty motorbike ride in Sirajganj. There are no known comorbidities. He denies any visual changes, deep eye pain, or discharge. On examination, a localized, tender, erythematous lump about 4 mm on the right upper eyelid was observed, with surrounding mild edema. Vitals: BP 129/77 mmHg, pulse 70 bpm, weight 68 kg. Assessment: Hordeolum. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to use a warm compress four times a day, avoid squeezing the lump, and avoid eye makeup. Follow-up: 1 week.

Visit note | 2025-01-13 09:00 AM | Dr. Tahmina Begum, Dermatology | Patient: Liton Awal, 24, male. The patient presents seeking treatment for facial pimples, blackheads, and the dark marks left behind after they heal. He works as a security guard and reports that his skin has become worse since working in a hot kitchen in Mymensingh. He has a history of Hypothyroidism. He denies using any new cosmetic products or taking oral steroids. On examination, there are about 23 inflamed spots on the face along with multiple open and closed comedones. Vitals: BP 116/80 mmHg, pulse 82 bpm, weight 65 kg. Assessment: Acne vulgaris. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to wash his face twice daily with a gentle cleanser and not to squeeze the spots. Follow-up: 2 months.

Visit note | 2025-01-13 10:00 AM | Dr. Fahmida Yasmin, ENT | Patient: Tamim Faruque, 25, male. The patient presents with recurrent fits of sneezing, itchy eyes, and nasal symptoms that worsen significantly in dusty environments. He works as a sales representative and notes that his symptoms have been worse since road construction began near his home in Narayanganj. He has a history of Essential hypertension. He denies any fever, sore throat, or thick discolored nasal discharge. On examination, his nasal turbinates are pale and boggy. Vitals: about 7 sneezing fits a day, BP 149/87 mmHg, pulse 71 bpm, weight 93 kg. Assessment: Allergic rhinitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to avoid dust, wear a mask when cleaning, and wash his bedding weekly. Follow-up: 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-01-13 10:30 AM | Dr. Shamima Nasrin, Ophthalmology | Patient: Rezaul Haque, 74, male. The patient presents with gritty and burning eye symptoms that worsen in air conditioning. Interestingly, he presents atypically with eyes that water all day rather than feeling dry. He is a madrasa teacher, and these symptoms began after long gaming sessions at home in Mohammadpur. There are no comorbidities. He denies any changes in his vision, eye pain, or sticky discharge. On examination, conjunctival injection was absent, but a tear break-up time 5 seconds was measured. Vitals: BP 112/84 mmHg, pulse 83 bpm, weight 85 kg. Assessment: Dry eye syndrome. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to look away from the screen every 20 minutes, blink often, and use a humidifier. Follow-up: 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-01-13 03:00 PM | Dr. Mehedi Hasan, Ophthalmology | Patient: Sabbir Shikder, 50, male. The patient complains of gritty, burning eyes associated with long hours of screen time. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to look away from the screen every 20 minutes, blink often, and use a humidifier. Follow-up: 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-01-13 03:30 PM | Dr. Habibur Rahman, Orthopedics | Patient: Bushra Mollah, 48, female. The patient presents with significant night pain in her shoulder and an inability to raise her arm fully. Follow-up: 4 weeks with a physiotherapy review.

Visit note | 2025-01-14 04:00 PM | Dr. Saiful Alam, Endocrinology | Patient: Orin Hossain, 70, female. Mrs. Hossain reports that she has been feeling constantly thirsty and has noticed that minor cuts on her skin are taking an unusually long time to heal. She is a retired civil servant, and these issues were first noted when her high blood sugar was found during a routine test before a trip to Mirpur. She has a history of Hypothyroidism for which she is on regular treatment. She denies any chest pain, shortness of breath, blurry vision, or numbness in her extremities. On physical examination, her vitals are: fasting glucose 9.5 mmol/L, BP 128/75 mmHg, pulse 75 bpm, weight 69 kg. Her chest is clear on auscultation, and her feet show no active ulcers. Assessment: Type 2 diabetes mellitus. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to reduce rice portions and sweets, walk briskly 30 minutes five days a week, check fasting sugar twice weekly, and check her feet daily. Follow-up in 3 months with HbA1c.

Visit note | 2025-01-14 04:00 PM | Dr. Asif Mahmud, Dermatology | Patient: Habiba Dewan, 19, female. Miss Dewan presents with dry, itchy skin and complains of intense scratching at night. She notes that her symptoms are significantly worse in winter. She works as a police constable, and her skin issues flared during the dry winter in Tangail. She has a comorbidity of Type 2 diabetes mellitus. She denies any joint pains, fever, or breathing difficulties. On physical examination, there is an erythematous, dry plaque on her arm with the affected area about 7 cm across. Other vitals are: BP 134/85 mmHg, pulse 89 bpm, weight 58 kg. Assessment: Atopic eczema. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to use a mild soap, avoid hot baths, and wear cotton clothes. Follow-up in 2 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-01-14 04:30 PM | Dr. Imran Kabir, Gastroenterology | Patient: Habiba Mondal, 29, female. Ms. Mondal presents to the clinic complaining of a sudden onset of loose watery stools and feeling extremely weak, which has persisted for the last forty-eight hours. She describes the stools as being entirely liquid, occurring approximately eight to ten times a day, which has left her severely fatigued and drained of energy. She works as a cricket coach, and she notes that these symptoms began after a picnic in Khulna where she consumed various local catered foods. She reports that several of her colleagues who attended the same event have also experienced similar mild stomach issues, though her symptoms seem to be the most severe. She has no known comorbidities and is not on any regular medications. On further questioning, she denies experiencing any high-grade fever, chills, persistent vomiting, or severe localized abdominal pain. She also confirms there is no visible blood or mucus in her stool. On physical examination, the patient appears visibly tired and has dry lips and oral mucosa, indicating mild to moderate dehydration. Her abdomen is soft and flat, with generalized mild tenderness on palpation, particularly around the periumbilical region, but there is no guarding or rigidity. Bowel sounds are hyperactive. Her vitals reveal a pulse 113 bpm, which is elevated, BP 129/86 mmHg, and a weight of 61 kg. Assessment: Acute gastroenteritis. Plan: a prescription was issued. The patient was strongly advised to focus on oral rehydration therapy by drinking small sips of fluid often, such as oral rehydration salts (ORS) and clean water, to replace lost electrolytes. She is recommended to stick to a bland diet and eat rice, bananas, and toast while avoiding dairy, spicy, and oily foods until her bowel movements normalize. Strict hand hygiene was discussed, and she must wash hands before eating and after using the washroom. Follow-up is advised in 2 days if the stools do not settle, or sooner if she develops a high fever, persistent vomiting, or inability to keep fluids down.

Visit note | 2025-01-15 10:00 AM | Dr. Moinul Haque, Neurology | Patient: Jahid Kabir, 73, male. Mr. Kabir presents complaining of nausea with a spinning sensation and dizziness whenever he looks up. Visit note | 2025-01-15 10:00 AM | Dr. Mahbuba Rahman, Psychiatry | Patient: Tushar Kundu, 51, male. Mr. Kundu reports waking up tired and having significant trouble falling asleep most nights.
